meta.title: The pupillary light response as a physiological index of aphantasia, sensory and phenomenological imagery strength
meta.domain: Cognitive neuroscience / psychophysics — objective (pupillometric) measurement of mental imagery and aphantasia
meta.overview: Uses the pupillary light response as an objective physiological index of visual imagery: imagining bright vs dark stimuli modulates pupil size in proportion to imagery strength (validated against binocular-rivalry priming), and individuals with aphantasia show no imagery-driven pupil response despite intact perceptual pupil responses and load-driven dilation — the first physiological validation of aphantasia.
meta.abstract: The pupillary light response indexes visual mental imagery: in the general population, imagining bright versus dark objects modulates pupil size, and the magnitude correlates with objective (binocular-rivalry) imagery strength and trial-by-trial vividness. Individuals with aphantasia show no significant imagery-driven pupillary light response, while their perceptual pupil response and cognitive-load-driven dilation are intact, providing the first physiological validation of aphantasia.

claims.statement: The imagery pupillary light response tracks objective sensory imagery strength (correlates with binocular-rivalry priming).
Trial-by-trial phenomenological vividness of visual imagery is tracked by the imagery pupillary light response.
Individuals with aphantasia show no significant imagery pupillary light response (evidence for the null).
Aphantasic individuals retain perceptual pupil light responses and load-driven pupil dilation (set-size effect).
The pupillary light response provides the first physiological validation of aphantasia.

contributions.typing_rationale: Establishes the imagery pupillary light response as an objective, involuntary physiological index of imagery strength, validated against binocular-rivalry priming — a measurement advance over self-report.
First physiological demonstration that aphantasics lack the imagery-driven pupil response while retaining perceptual and load responses, providing objective validation of the condition.

sota.resolver_notes: Undermind semantic search (year_max=2022) identified Laeng & Sulutvedt 2014 (pupil adjusts to imagined light) as the direct methodological parent, extended here to imagery strength and aphantasia; Keogh & Pearson 2018 (objective absence of imagery) and Pearson 2008 (rivalry/imagery method) are the aphantasia-measurement priors. The physiological validation of aphantasia has no close precedent — moderate neighborhood, method-level overlap.
